document_preamble:
# {Feature Name} Design Doc

**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Version:** v1
**Status:** Draft

**Document References:**
- Decision-doc: `{/<cycle_id>/tech/diagnostic/decision-doc.md}`

**Chain domain:** Technical solution design (技术方案设计) — design sign-off before tech-plan; not enterprise architecture, not execution specs. Register rules and audience: see domain-instance.

---

CTX.heading: Context
CTX.intent: Problem domain for the design: why now (trigger), verified current state, relevant system surfaces, external dependency facts, and reference implementations or patterns to mirror when decision points to them. Include the user-perceived or system-level impact of the current state — not only the code or structural description of what exists, but what problem or cost it causes. Lead with problem-domain narrative (trigger and current state in reviewable prose) before optional concrete anchors; code or path facts support the story, they do not replace it.
CTX.intent_boundary: Solution selection, structural layout, module partitioning, interface fields, key decisions, verification commands, and tasks belong to GO, ST, KD, IF, VD, OD, and tech-plan. Enterprise architecture redesign and platform restructuring are out of scope unless authorized in decision-doc.
CTX.guidance: Problem-domain narrative first (trigger and current state in reviewable prose); optional concrete anchors support the story; compact opening arc; no structure diagrams.

required: Opens with problem-domain narrative before path or code inventories
States user-perceived or system-behavior consequence, not code structure alone
forbidden: Opening paragraphs that lead with file:line or DOM id chains
Describing the current state solely through code structure or component names without stating user-perceived or system-behavior consequence
Scope or exclusion tables
Structure or flow diagrams
Checkbox steps, Run commands, or phase markers

GO.heading: Design Outcomes
GO.intent: Observable success state reviewers can agree on when design is sufficient: before→after at behavior or structure level. May reference acceptance criteria semantically without tracing them to tasks or commands.
GO.intent_boundary: Background facts belong to CTX. Exclusions belong to NG. Scope surface belongs to SC. Module layout belongs to ST. Phases, checkboxes, SK/T, metric thresholds, and Run commands belong to tech-plan.
GO.guidance: Observable before→after success state; operationalize the problem CTX established; compact outcomes prose.

required: Opens by operationalizing the CTX transitional connection — do not jump directly to before/after enumeration without establishing the design response
forbidden: Background narrative duplicating CTX
Scope tables or architecture diagrams

SC.heading: Scope
SC.intent: Functional, module, interface, and data surfaces this design covers — what is in play for this feature.
SC.intent_boundary: Explicit out-of-scope and rejected directions belong to NG. Invariants belong to I. File-level change lists and tasks belong to tech-plan.
SC.guidance: Functional, module, interface, and data surfaces in play; tables preferred over prose when enumerating.

required: Surfaces covered by this design in structured or tabular form when more than two items
forbidden: Checkable invariants list (belongs in I)
Exclusion essays (belongs in NG)

NG.heading: Non-Goals
NG.intent: Paths and capabilities explicitly not chosen or not pursued — directional exclusions that protect the design outcome, including paths explicitly rejected during design collaboration.
NG.intent_boundary: Scope touch-surface tables belong to SC. Trade-off rationale and rejected-option analysis belong to KD. Task deferrals belong to tech-plan.
NG.guidance: Directional exclusions protecting the design outcome; when mixing out-of-scope and rejected directions, use a table distinguishing nature (out-of-scope / rejected direction) and protected boundary.

required: Each exclusion identifies what design boundary or success state it protects
forbidden: Trade-off or rejected-option comparison essays (belongs in KD)
Interface contract tables

I.heading: Invariants
I.intent: Checkable statements that must remain true in the intended running system — including constraint-grade user priors from decision-doc, not implementation tricks or runbook steps.
I.intent_boundary: Option comparisons belong to KD. Interface contracts belong to IF. Runbooks and operational steps belong to OD strategy only or tech-plan.
I.guidance: Checkable invariant list as primary carrier.

required: Checkable invariants as a list when present
forbidden: Phase tables or checkbox steps

ST.heading: Structure
ST.intent: Placement within the existing system, modules or components, responsibilities, dependency direction, cross-boundary data or control flow, relationship to existing assets, and structure-level behavior inside components — including named states, transition triggers, and path end-state semantics where interaction or control flow is non-obvious, sufficient for IF and tech-plan without re-deriving behavior.
ST.intent_boundary: Field-level API contracts belong to IF. Selected or rejected approaches belong to KD. Execution order, file edit lists, and task steps belong to tech-plan. Enterprise architecture or platform-level restructuring is out of scope unless decision-doc authorizes it only for instantiation.
ST.guidance: When design changes user interaction or component state, make state/path behavior scannable: named states, transition triggers, and path end-states must be explicit. Use the lightest structured view that removes inference (named-state prose, comparison tables, path tables, or diagrams) — do not default to diagrams when narrative or tables suffice. When the design involves more than three components with non-obvious dependency directions, lead with a system-level diagram (Mermaid flowchart or tool-agnostic equivalent) before the component responsibility table; the diagram covers system placement and data-flow direction, the table covers component responsibilities — do not duplicate between them.

required: When design changes interaction or component state: explicit named states, transition triggers, and path end-states in a structured view (tool-agnostic)
When cross-boundary paths are non-obvious: explicit trigger-to-boundary path in a structured view (tool-agnostic)
forbidden: Field-level API or schema tables
Rejected-option essays
Checkbox steps or file edit lists
Decorative diagrams without behavioral semantics
Diagram-only blocks that omit named states or end-states when interaction or state changes

KD.heading: Key Decisions
KD.intent: Human-adopted design choices, rejected alternatives with rationale (including explicitly rejected AI-proposed paths), confirmed design premises, and design-level choices such as reversibility and data semantics. Before option comparison, state the core design insight — the key realization or principle that makes the chosen approach valid. Rationale for each adopted direction must distinguish between external constraints (what was required or authorized by stakeholders) and design reasoning (why this approach is technically sound); citing external authorization alone does not constitute complete rationale.
KD.intent_boundary: Structural layout belongs to ST. Interface fields belong to IF. Phase tags, Done conditions, Must Close Before phase, Owner, and Timing belong to tech-plan or OQ without project metadata.
KD.guidance: Decision-comparison prose or table; chosen vs rejected paths readable without rereading Solution Shape.

required: Decision comparison table or equivalent structured comparison when multiple paths were considered
forbidden: Adopted direction rationale consisting solely of stakeholder authorization references without design reasoning
Module graph or dependency diagrams duplicating Solution Shape
Interface field tables
Phase tags, Done conditions, Owner, or Timing tables

IF.heading: Interfaces
IF.intent: Cross-module contracts: APIs, events, data schemas, naming conventions, error semantics, and compatibility expectations — verifiable at semantic level.
IF.intent_boundary: Module graph and dependency direction belong to ST. Implementation steps, change items, and concrete file patches belong to tech-plan.
IF.guidance: Cross-boundary interface semantics in structured, field-aligned form; do not infer contracts from structure prose in prior blocks.

required: Cross-boundary semantics in structured, field-aligned form when more than one field or endpoint (tool-agnostic)
forbidden: Module responsibility prose duplicating Solution Shape
Implementation steps or file patches

OQ.heading: Open Questions
OQ.intent: Unresolved assumptions, open questions, and risk statements not yet closed; each item labeled blocks-plan or non-blocking. May include design-level mitigation thinking, not execution tasks.
OQ.intent_boundary: Closed decisions belong to KD. Verification commands, Owner, Timing, and task linkage belong to tech-plan. SK/T/VF content must not appear here.
OQ.guidance: Unresolved assumptions and risks; each item labeled blocks-plan or non-blocking; identify design assumption left open, not implementation uncertainty alone.

required: blocks-plan or non-blocking label on each row
forbidden: Run commands, test file paths, or checkbox steps
SK/T/VF-style phase or task tables
OQ item descriptions that state only an implementation uncertainty without identifying the design assumption or dimension it leaves open

VD.heading: Verification Design
VD.intent: How the design will be proven correct at review time: test strategy (unit, integration, E2E division), semantic AC-to-verification mapping, and assumptions that must close before downstream execution planning — cross-linked to OQ. Include at least one falsifiability condition: what observable outcome or behavior would indicate the design assumption is wrong or incomplete.
VD.intent_boundary: Run commands, test file paths, checkbox steps, and Owner/Timing tables belong to downstream execution documents only. Success state definition belongs to GO.
VD.guidance: Test strategy and AC mapping; cross-reference OQ assumptions; include falsifiable pass signal per verification method; when shared modal or multi-panel UI, state semantic regression scope for sibling flows (no Run commands).

required: Each verification method includes a distinguishable pass signal — what a passing result looks like, not only the action performed
forbidden: Run commands or test file paths

OD.heading: Operability & Release Design
OD.intent: Design-level operability and release: what to observe and health criteria, gradual rollout strategy decisions, degradation and failure semantics, rollback and data-repair strategy — not runbooks or scripts.
OD.intent_boundary: Metric thresholds, alert configs, rollout runbooks, switch procedures, and repair scripts belong to downstream execution or ops documents only. Structural decisions belong to ST/KD.
OD.guidance: Rollout, degradation, rollback, and observability strategy at design level — not runbooks.

forbidden: Run commands, test file paths, or checkbox steps
Runbooks, metric threshold tables, or repair scripts
